title: Cyber liability insurance (first and third party)
status_rationale: No insurance policy, certificate, quotation or broker engagement was located. Business plan section 14.07 states a draft position on insurance and risk transfer only.
target_answer: Echelon carries cyber liability insurance from an admitted carrier rated A- or better by AM Best, covering first-party costs (forensics, notification, credit monitoring, data restoration, business interruption including dependent business interruption from cloud and AI providers, extortion) and third-party liability (privacy and network security claims, regulatory defense and fines where insurable, media liability). Limits are set from a broker-supported analysis of the largest contractual commitments and plausible loss scenarios rather than chosen in advance, and are increased before onboarding customers whose contracts require more. Exclusions and minimum-security warranties are reviewed against our actual controls.
current_practice: Unknown; no evidence of any policy.
intended_practice: Engage a broker and bind cyber coverage before the first production customer.
customer_statement: Echelon does not currently hold a cyber insurance policy that we can evidence. We plan to bind cyber coverage before handling customer production data.
open_questions: What cyber limits are realistically available to a pre-revenue Indiana LLC without a SOC report, and at what premium?

title: Technology errors and omissions (professional liability)
status_rationale: No insurance policy, certificate, quotation or broker engagement was located. Business plan section 14.07 states a draft position on insurance and risk transfer only.
target_answer: Echelon carries technology errors and omissions insurance, typically combined with cyber in one tower, covering financial loss to customers from errors in the service, including miscalculation of fees, balances, NAV or grant amounts and errors in AI-assisted outputs. title: Crime, fidelity and social engineering coverage matched to the service's loss scenarios
status_rationale: No insurance policy, certificate, quotation or broker engagement was located. Business plan section 14.07 states a draft position on insurance and risk transfer only. Unbound's design states it never holds or moves funds and cannot execute payments (CNV-LEG-001), which changes which crime losses it can cause.
target_answer: Echelon carries commercial crime coverage including employee dishonesty, third-party (client property) coverage, computer fraud, funds transfer fraud and social engineering, with limits based on the loss scenarios the service can actually cause. Because Unbound prepares but does not execute payments and never holds funds, the dominant insurable scenario is a fraudulent payment instruction prepared through the platform and released by the sponsor; we document this scenario and coordinate coverage with the sponsor's own crime policy so there is no gap between them.
intended_practice: Bind crime coverage with third-party extension; document loss scenarios with the broker.
customer_statement: Crime and fidelity coverage is not currently in place. The platform is designed not to hold or move customer funds.

challenge.customer_intent: Recovery if vendor personnel or attackers cause theft of the customer's funds.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Fraudulent grant payments or diverted funds.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Crime insurance compensates after the fact; it does not prevent loss and often has low social engineering sublimits.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in financial services vendor contracts, especially for vendors with access to payment systems.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Unbound never holds funds and cannot execute payments (CNV-LEG-001); payee bank changes and releases require sponsor authority with separation of duties.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Authority matrix refuses unmapped commands (CNV-GOV-010); payee change notifications (CNV-PLT-011).
challenge.stronger_alternative: Architectural prevention plus coordinated, not duplicated, coverage.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially; design is verifiable once built and tested.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any path by which Echelon personnel or agents can alter payee data or release payments.
challenge.alternative_cost: Engineering cost already within product scope.
challenge.alternative_risks: Residual social engineering of sponsor staff is not prevented by architecture.
supporting_arguments: Reduces the probability of the insured event, not only its cost.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; procurement checklists often require crime coverage regardless of architecture.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Insurance is still the expected backstop and costs little relative to the risk.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: General liability, workers compensation, D&O, umbrella and key-person coverage
status_rationale: No insurance policy, certificate, quotation or broker engagement was located. Business plan section 14.07 states a draft position on insurance and risk transfer only. Whether Echelon has employees (relevant to workers compensation) is unknown.
target_answer: Echelon carries commercial general liability, workers compensation and employer's liability as required by state law once it has employees, an umbrella policy over general and employer's liability, management liability (D&O) once there are outside investors or a board, and key-person life and disability insurance on the founder payable to the company and earmarked in the wind-down plan to fund an orderly customer transition.

title: Contractual insurance terms: additional insured, certificates, notice, carrier quality and shared limits
status_rationale: No insurance policy, certificate, quotation or broker engagement was located. Business plan section 14.07 states a draft position on insurance and risk transfer only.
target_answer: We provide certificates of insurance at signing and on each renewal, name customers as additional insured on general liability and where available on cyber third-party coverage, agree to waiver of subrogation and primary and non-contributory wording where carriers permit, give 30 days' notice of cancellation, non-renewal or material reduction, and use carriers rated A- or better by AM Best. We disclose that cyber and E&O limits are aggregate limits shared across all customers and size them accordingly.
intended_practice: Track certificates and endorsements per customer.
customer_statement: Certificates and endorsements cannot be provided until coverage is bound.

title: Claims history, adequacy of limits and accuracy of underwriting representations
status_rationale: No insurance policy, certificate, quotation or broker engagement was located. Business plan section 14.07 states a draft position on insurance and risk transfer only. Without policies there is no claims history to report; there is also no record of any application.
target_answer: We disclose five-year loss runs from our carriers and any declined, rescinded or non-renewed coverage. Limits are set from a documented analysis linking contractual liability, plausible loss scenarios and customer requirements. Security representations in insurance applications are generated from the same control evidence used for customer due diligence and reviewed against it before submission, so that coverage cannot be rescinded for misrepresentation; insurer-required controls (for example MFA, backups, endpoint detection) are tracked as obligations with evidence.
intended_practice: Build insurance applications from this repository's answer units and evidence.
customer_statement: Echelon has no insurance claims history that can be evidenced because no coverage is currently evidenced. Insurance applications will be answered from the same verified control records used for customer due diligence.

challenge.customer_intent: Insurance will actually pay when needed and is sized to the risk.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Coverage is denied or rescinded because the application overstated controls, or limits are far below the loss.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Customers check only certificates; certificates do not reveal exclusions, warranties or misrepresentation risk.
challenge.contractually_required: Certificates and minimum limits are commonly required; application accuracy is rarely examined.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Application answers generated from answer units whose statuses are validated.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Single source of truth for security representations to insurers and customers.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by comparing submitted applications to answer unit history.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.alternative_risks: Honest applications for a startup may raise premiums or reduce available limits.
supporting_arguments: Prevents rescission, which is the worst insurance failure for a customer.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely; it strengthens rather than replaces certificates.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Customers have little visibility into application content.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.
